The codebase has two distinct `audit-issues.json` finding-shape conventions: auditor-style and reviewer-style.

Auditor-style findings (used by `review-architecture-auditor`, `review-cross-artifact-auditor`) have shape `{id, severity, category, summary, evidence[], recommended_resolution}` with severity in `{BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR, INFO}`; schema lives in agent prompts (not in `auditing-shared`).

Reviewer-style findings (used by `shared-document-reviewer` + documented in `KB-review-disciplines/references/severity-taxonomy.md`) have the same shape but severity in `{critical, important, recommended}` + category in `{consistency, completeness, compliance, clarity, feasibility}` (a separate dimension).
NFR-8's prescribed `rule / target / divergence / next_action` fields are not in either current schema; they are additive.
Auditor agents (architecture, cross-artifact) use severity vocabulary `BLOCKER / MAJOR / MINOR / INFO`.
`auditing-mcp` SKILL.md "Severity meanings (v2)" uses vocabulary `BLOCKER / MAJOR / MINOR / NIT` (NIT not INFO — slight divergence).
`shared-document-reviewer` + KB-review-disciplines use severity vocabulary `critical / important / recommended`.
`test-phase-validator-author` Phase 2 uses severity vocabulary `blocking / warning / informational`.
`auditing-cc-configs/scripts/verdict_compute.py` bridges the auditor vocabulary into point deductions (`BLOCKER -12, MAJOR -5, MINOR -2, NIT -0.5, INFO 0`).
PRD AC text for FR-1/4/5/9/10 uses the auditor vocabulary explicitly (BLOCKER / MAJOR).
